# The Great Create x Cricut Artist Feature: Mackenzie Brittingham


-
-
-


6 October 2026


[Mackenzie Brittingham](https://cricut.com/blog/author/mbrittingham/)


---


At[Mackenzie Brittingham](http://mackenziebrittingham.com/) , so much of what we create begins with fabric, imagination, and a love for the smallest details. From hand-beaded embellishments to dimensional silk flowers, so many elements of our couture garments are thoughtfully designed and crafted in our Dallas studio.


This year, we are so excited to bring a little piece of that creative process to the[Nasher Sculpture Center’s Great Create event](https://www.nashersculpturecenter.org/programs-events/the-great-create) , where we’ll have the opportunity to work with young artists to create a Textile Garden inspired by the techniques we use in our own couture work.


## Bringing our ideas to life with Cricut Maker 5


Floral embellishments have become a beautiful part of our design process. We create flowers from silk and other specialty fabrics in a variety of shapes and sizes. We then layer, bead, manipulate, and hand-attach each flower to our couture garments.


One tool that has made this process so much easier is our[Cricut Maker 5](https://cricut.com/en-us/cutting-machines/cricut-maker/cricut-maker-5/cricut-maker-5-essential-bundle/2012944.html) .


Instead of individually hand-cutting every flower, we can create our floral shapes digitally and use Cricut Maker 5 to precisely cut multiples from fabric. This allows our team to continue working on the many other hand-finished elements of a garment while still achieving beautifully consistent flower shapes.


The Cricut Design Space app also makes it incredibly easy to adjust our designs. We can scale a flower up or down depending on a client’s specifications, the proportions of a gown, or simply what we feel will look most beautiful within a particular design. We can create tiny flowers for delicate details, larger statement blooms, or an entire collection of varying sizes to give a garment dimension and movement.


Once the pieces are cut, that’s where the couture handwork begins. We can layer the petals, shape them, add beading and embellishment, and finally hand-attach each finished flower to the garment.


## Growing our textile garden


For our activity at the Nasher Sculpture Center’s Great Create event, we wanted to take our Cricut-cut flowers and turn them into something children could experience and make completely their own.


Our Textile Garden will begin with canvases and an assortment of scrap fabrics saved from our studio. Rather than letting those beautiful remnants go to waste, we’ll transform them into flowers, petals, leaves, and other garden-inspired shapes.


Some pieces will be hand-cut, and others will be cut using Cricut Maker 5, giving the children a variety of textile elements to choose from. From there, they’ll get to become the designers.


Each child can arrange, layer, mix, and attach the fabric pieces onto a canvas to create their own one-of-a-kind textile garden. Just like designing a couture gown, there is no single “right” way to create it. A tiny scrap of silk can become a petal, different textures can be layered together, and flowers can grow into whatever shape their imagination allows.


What we love most about this project is that it connects so many things that are important to us: fashion, art, technology, craftsmanship, sustainability, and creativity.


Cricut helps us take an idea from a digital shape to a physical piece of fabric, and from there, creativity takes over. Just like a needle and thread, the Cricut Maker 5 is another tool that helps us bring our ideas to life. Whether that flower is being hand-beaded for a couture gown or arranged by a young artist onto a canvas, it helps create the pieces, while each person’s imagination and hands make the final result completely their own.


We cannot wait to see the gardens they grow.

## About[Mackenzie Brittingham](https://cricut.com/blog/author/mbrittingham/)


[http://mackenziebrittingham.com](http://mackenziebrittingham.com/)


Mackenzie Brittingham is a Dallas-based designer and founder of her namesake luxury atelier, recognized for custom couture, bridal, eveningwear, luxury outerwear, and bespoke accessories. Known for a highly personalized design experience and an unwavering commitment to craftsmanship, Brittingham creates one-of-a-kind pieces tailored to life’s most meaningful moments—from weddings and galas to philanthropic events, milestone celebrations, and private commissions. Her work spans custom bridal gowns, mother-of-the-bride and bridesmaid dressing, debutante presentations, cocktail attire, black-tie eveningwear, day-to-night wardrobe pieces, and specialty occasion dressing. In addition to couture apparel, Brittingham also offers custom fur designs, statement outerwear, and an evolving line of handcrafted luxury handbags and accessories. Celebrated for refined silhouettes, exceptional fit, and globally sourced textiles, Brittingham blends timeless elegance with modern femininity. Drawing inspiration from travel, architecture, old-world glamour, and Italian craftsmanship, each design is developed through an intimate collaborative process that honors both the client and the artistry of the garment. A longtime supporter of Dallas’ philanthropic and cultural communities, Brittingham’s designs have been featured at many of the city’s most prominent galas, charitable events, weddings, and social occasions. Through her growing atelier, she continues to shape a new chapter of bespoke luxury fashion in Texas while mentoring emerging creatives and championing craftsmanship for the next generation.
